title: The LIFE School.
subtitle: A self-directed school where students make their own path. I helped redesign its website so parents and students could find their next step.
role: UX Designer (team: Jarrett Coger, lead; Treven Holcomb, UX)

glance.Problem: The site lacked direction, so parents and students had trouble identifying their next steps.
glance.Contribution: UX on a three-person team: research, personas, site map and wireframes.
glance.Outcome: A clearer, consolidated site with an easier application process.

hero.caption: Wireframe example of The LIFE School 2.0 website

sections.label: Overview
sections.heading: Everything is catered towards the student.
paras: The LIFE School is self-directed: students shape their own paths. The website needed to reflect that and guide families toward what to do next.

sections.label: Problem statement
sections.heading: Visitors had no clear next step.
paras: The website lacked direction. Without guidance, parents and students had trouble identifying what to do next.

sections.label: User interviews
sections.heading: Freedom of choice is what excites students.
bullets: Students were more excited about the freedom of choice at this school than at their previous schools.
Most students learned about the school from adults in their lives, not from their own research.

sections.label: Competitive analysis
sections.heading: Every competing school specializes in something.
bullets: Each competing school specializes in something particular.
Most schools focus heavily on Admissions and About us, with other content treated as secondary.

sections.label: Web comparative analysis
sections.heading: What the best school sites do well.
bullets: All the sites present their identity clearly.
They use abundant photos and videos of students and their activities.
Text-heavy pages are broken into more digestible sections.
Each site has at least one unique feature.
Sites emphasize giving and applying, making those options easy to find.

sections.label: Personas
sections.heading: Different people, overlapping pain points.
paras: The personas are modeled on the adults and students we interviewed. Their pain points overlap, centering on a desire for more growth, focus, and attention.

sections.label: Discovery
sections.heading: The site was dense, with information spread across many pages.
paras: Research showed the site was very dense, with information spread across several pages.

sections.label: Wireframes
sections.heading: Wireframes for The LIFE School 2.0.
paras: The hero image above is the home page wireframe from the redesign.

results: The site was consolidated from 25 pages down to 6 long pages with clear directions.
The application process is easier to navigate.
